newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka oil refinery to shutdown for a week.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka oil refinery to shutdown for a week.

COLOMBO, May 26 (Reuter) - Sri Lanka's only crude oil refinery, run by the state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), will have an unscheduled shutdown shortly for about a week, the company chairman said. "There's not enough crude to run the refinery after our mooring buoy, which discharges crude from tankers, was damaged in an accident last week," CPC chairman Anil Obeyesekere told Reuters.

Other CPC officials said the shutdown will begin later this week or early next week. Obeyesekere said the CPC will import more refined products to meet the shortfall caused by the shutdown of the refinery which can refine 50,000-60,000 barrels per day.

"There's no way customers will get affected because we have enough products and we're importing extra parcels of gas oil and diesel," he said. "One tanker is unloading at the moment, another one is coming this week and a further one will be here by June 10."
The crude shortage was caused by damage to the CPC's Single Point Mooring Buoy, a few kilometers off Colombo port, last week. The buoy is meant for crude oil tankers too big to enter Colombo port.

Discharge of crude oil came to a halt last Tuesday after a tanker collided with and damaged the buoy in bad weather. "The hose was damaged in the accident. So we can't discharge crude from the tanker," Obeyesekere said. "We're getting a new hose from Dubai."
